hero.headline: 40-year-old driver killed in head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County
hero.body:
A 40-year-old man was killed early Sunday after a head-on crash on State Road 710 in Martin County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 2 a.m. near State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, and Southwest Silver Fox Lane. FHP said a 2015 Kia Optima was traveling north on State Road 710 when the driver crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The front left of the Kia struck the front left of the Tundra. Upon impact, the Kia burst into flames and came to rest on the grass shoulder facing north. The Tundra came to rest facing southeast in the southbound lane. The driver of the Kia, a 40-year-old man, died at the scene. The driver of the Tundra, a 41-year-old man from Indiantown, was taken to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter.

Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 just this year. After a fatal crash in January, Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek called the road a death trap. Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry… just living here makes me worry about the young people learning to drive and learning to drive on that road concerns me, because I have young kids."

The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen the road from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes.

Townsend said faster action is needed. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said.

cards.headline: State Road 710 widening project delayed until 2031 despite safety concerns
cards.teaser: Construction to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four will not begin until 2031, according to the Florida Department of Transportation.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. The delay has drawn criticism from Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek, particularly after multiple fatal crashes on the roadway. Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 this year alone. After a fatal crash in January, Budensiek called the road a "death trap." The most recent fatality occurred early Sunday morning when a 40-year-old man died in a head-on collision near Southwest Silver Fox Lane around 2 a.m.

According to the Florida Highway Patrol, a 2015 Kia Optima traveling north on State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The Kia burst into flames upon impact and came to rest on the grass shoulder. The driver died at the scene. The 41-year-old driver of the Tundra from Indiantown was transported to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter. The crash highlights ongoing safety concerns about the two-lane road.

Sheriff Budensiek has questioned how long residents must wait for improvements given the road's track record. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents and described driver behavior as reckless. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry."

In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes. However, Townsend said faster action is needed beyond these interim measures. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said. Townsend also expressed concern about young drivers learning to navigate the dangerous roadway, noting he has young children. The 2031 timeline for widening the road means nearly a decade will pass before major construction begins to address the safety issues that have made State Road 710 one of the most dangerous roads in Martin County.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with international residency program
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce preserves the historic Crain Estate while offering artist residencies and art classes to residents of all skill levels in the Peacock Arts District.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists. Located in the historic Crain Estate, the non-profit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The estate remains 90% the way it was when the Crains lived there. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven birds originally that have grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognized because he walks with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Krystal Masters, the art director, leads one-on-one classes where students come in with zero experience and walk out with a piece of art.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent as inflation hits holiday food prices
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July tradition of cookouts, grilling and picnics comes with a higher price tag this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation as the cause of rising prices. Ground beef is up 5.5 percent, and buns are up 7.7 percent. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4 percent. Ice cream is up 5.3 percent.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. These lower prices on select items provide some relief for shoppers planning their holiday celebrations, though the overall trend shows an increase in costs compared to last year.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check despite the rising prices. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said. Her advice emphasizes the importance of strategic shopping and planning ahead to make the most of grocery budgets during the holiday.

Local shoppers described their plans for Fourth of July meals despite the higher costs. One shopper said Friday they were planning hamburgers, unfortunately not on the grill because they live in a condo, with coleslaw, chips and maybe some beer for lunch. For dinner, they planned burnt ends, mashed potatoes and fresh broccoli. Another shopper said they were cooking hamburgers, beef, steak and baked potato for their celebration. The varied menu plans show families are still committed to traditional holiday meals even as inflation affects grocery prices across multiple food categories.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie expands Midway Road and adds Florida Turnpike interchange to accommodate growth
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to build a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road, addressing a significant gap between current entrances and exits.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council last month approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in the city.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are working on the first phase widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027.

The project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. Erin Scheumeister, a Port St. Lucie resident, said the construction can be annoying but believes it is necessary. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit rescued two boaters Wednesday after their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman killed in home fire as community rallies to support surviving fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home, with preliminary findings from the sheriff's office pointing to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, spoke exclusively about the loss and said she learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiancé Mark, who told her that Misty had passed away in a fire. Fenn returned to the scene in the days following the tragedy to process her grief.

Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his one and only child, Jacob, tragically. Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening and plants and plays the piano, and she was always the first to lend a hand. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, meaning she passed just a few days before her birthday, adding another layer of heartbreak for those who knew her.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem Blue Cross denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield deny coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled, citing the GalaFlex mesh as investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She had a full double bilateral mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational and there is no or not enough proof it improves health. GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh that is not FDA-approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational, and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated that its efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined.

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says the product is giving her patients the least amount of complications. Billington recently shared Clark's denial on social media and took part in a viral dance with friends to call for policy changes. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Despite her insurer's denial, Clark got her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago thanks to Billington finding a mechanism to make that happen. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes for $3 million renovation that will nearly double slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock closed July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees and will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms, noting the year of waiting will be worth it. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock for drop-off and pick-up. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, initially had concerns about whether it could continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock's non-floating section to board passengers there. Kuyrkendall said Stuart is not Stuart without the water and acknowledged the dock gets hectic on weekends when boats squeeze in to find spots. He said modernizing and expanding the dock will be great for the city and his business. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and he hopes they add more floating docks.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She said in an Instagram post that she is heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles and that the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to her. She said she did everything she could but her knee is not ready to compete.

The Instagram post included images of four syringes that Serena said shows the fluid they drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra. It was the only first-round doubles match that was not scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, saying to stay tuned to a city near you with the U.S. Open approaching. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina beats Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina survived a scare from underdog Cape Verde, winning 3-2 in extra time Friday to advance to the Round of 16.
cards.body:
Argentina's go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Messi scored early in regulation for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense in the 29th minute on a well-timed run as Lisandro Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead.

Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, 40 years old, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi.

Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday. Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappe in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer in this year's World Cup, and extended his World Cup record with 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for a state championship run during the fall 2026 season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district title. A second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year seniors, with the majority coming from the middle school program. They know how things are run and have experienced success throughout their careers. Robertson said he hopes their senior year will be the best season the program has had.

Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to take the program to the next level by creating a challenging schedule for this year. The goal is to compete by playing against really good teams, which also helps attract new people to the program. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs. While the team wants to go undefeated in the regular season, that does not matter if they keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as something to look forward to each day. Working harder during the offseason will allow the team to see positive results when the season arrives and break their record.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

hero.headline: State Road 710 widening project delayed until 2031 despite safety concerns
hero.teaser: Construction to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four will not begin until 2031, according to the Florida Department of Transportation.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation has plans to widen State Road 710 from two lanes to four, but construction is not expected to begin until 2031. The delay has drawn criticism from Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek, particularly after multiple fatal crashes on the roadway. Martin County Fire Rescue has responded to 42 vehicle accident-related calls on State Road 710 this year alone. After a fatal crash in January, Budensiek called the road a "death trap." The most recent fatality occurred early Sunday morning when a 40-year-old man died in a head-on collision near Southwest Silver Fox Lane around 2 a.m.

According to the Florida Highway Patrol, a 2015 Kia Optima traveling north on State Road 710, also known as Beeline Highway, crossed into the southbound lane and collided head-on with a 2021 Toyota Tundra. The Kia burst into flames upon impact and came to rest on the grass shoulder. The driver died at the scene. The 41-year-old driver of the Tundra from Indiantown was transported to the hospital via LifeStar medical helicopter. The crash highlights ongoing safety concerns about the two-lane road.

Sheriff Budensiek has questioned how long residents must wait for improvements given the road's track record. "The question will be how many more people have to die before we get that project going. Florida touts that they have the safest roads in the country but this road is one that clearly is not in that category," Budensiek said in January. Bill Townsend, who lives nearby, said the road has long been a concern for residents and described driver behavior as reckless. "People don't pay a whole lot of attention to other people on the road, and [it's] kind of a dangerous road sometimes," Townsend said. "Everybody's always in a hurry."

In the meantime, FDOT has begun improvements to the road, including pavement, markings, signage and new turn lanes. However, Townsend said faster action is needed beyond these interim measures. "It would be beneficial to the people that live and travel that road all the time if something happened faster," Townsend said. Townsend also expressed concern about young drivers learning to navigate the dangerous roadway, noting he has young children. The 2031 timeline for widening the road means nearly a decade will pass before major construction begins to address the safety issues that have made State Road 710 one of the most dangerous roads in Martin County.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination with global artists and historic Crain Estate
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists. Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the nonprofit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility. "Jackson is the one who did all the tiling throughout the facility, and you'll see it from the ground to the walls to the ceiling," says Krystal Masters, the art director. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.

The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate including a gazebo shipped from India. The estate remains largely unchanged from the Crains' time there. "It's 90% the way it was when the Crains were here," Krystal said. The foundation has made a conscious effort to preserve the estate's original character. Many parts of the house look the same as when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room. At one time, the Crains also kept monkeys on the property. According to foundation representatives, the story goes that Jackson Crain went to South America, got a baby monkey, stuck it in his pocket, and came home with it.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. "From what we hear, they brought in seven of them originally, and from the seven we have over 100," a foundation representative said. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old. "We do have one named Bob that we know of. We believe he's 60 years old and we know him because he walks with a limp," said Masters. Bob is hand fed every day by staff and has his own bowls.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The foundation's art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Masters leads one-on-one classes designed to be accessible to complete beginners. "The majority of my classes are one on one classes you come in with zero experience and you walk out with a piece of art and it makes you feel good," Krystal said. The art lab features a wide range of mediums and projects, including sculpting and watercolor. For Krystal, art serves a deeper purpose. "Art is a form of therapy and it distresses people," Krystal said.
